title: Faster PipeShare folders and video playback
description:
Opening a job in PipeShare was waiting on a full Wasabi folder listing plus database lookups before anything was drawn, and large folders could sit there for a long time. Videos were stored as a generic file type, so the browser often downloaded a big chunk of the file before it would play or seek.

Folder lists now paint the first page (one level, up to 1000 names) and load the rest in the background. Repeat opens reuse a short server cache. Video links tell Wasabi to answer as video/mp4 (or the real type) with range support, so playback can start and seek without pulling the whole file through the portal. The same code serves pipeshare.live and pipeshare.net.

Who is affected: PipeShare in the browser on the private server and SaaS. Desktop Auto Sync upload behavior is unchanged. Very large videos can still take a moment to show the first frame when the movie index is at the end of the file; seeking uses byte ranges instead of a full download.
changeLog: PipeShare draws the first folder page immediately and loads further pages in the background.
Shallow folder listings are cached briefly on the server so reopening a folder is quick.
Video and PDF links are presigned with the real content type and inline playback so the browser can range-request.
Wasabi buckets expose range headers for direct browser playback.
Nginx no longer buffers proxied file downloads, and API responses get larger memory buffers.
